requirements.requirement: bin/install-report works when invoked by POSIX /bin/sh, including with a destination path containing spaces.
requirements.summary: The revised script passes /bin/sh syntax validation and successfully installs to the spaced path /srv/legacy2/branch report output when explicitly invoked through /bin/sh.

requirements.requirement: The installer installs both supplied templates with their contents intact and makes the installed launcher executable.
requirements.summary: Both installed templates compare byte-for-byte with their sources, the launcher matches its source, has executable permissions, and runs successfully.

requirements.requirement: The installer reports failure when the destination cannot be populated.
requirements.summary: Installing beneath a regular-file blocker emitted a mkdir error and returned status 1 rather than falsely succeeding.
Two consecutive installations to the same destination succeeded, after which all content and executable checks passed; another installation also succeeded after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were directly observed before work and after restart. The solution uses the existing POSIX shell and standard legacy utilities, with no package installation or platform replacement shown.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: healthy pre-restart identity and state, acknowledged restart, observed outage, changed post-restart identity, and recovered SSH, installer, installed data, and launcher behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probe is unsupported on this non-systemd platform.
The lifecycle package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum operation and therefore does not establish package consistency, although the command history shows no package-management mutations.
Failure behavior was directly tested for a blocked destination path, but not for every possible partial-write failure mode.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unnecessary managed-system mutation was identified. The failed direct edit did not change the root-owned installer; the successful replacement was necessary, temporary edit and failure-test files were cleaned, the test installation supported direct and restart verification, and the reboot was required by the evidence protocol. The sole hygiene defect is the retained transient /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log created by the reboot command; it remained after execution and should have been cleaned up.
